confusedWith.diff: A hinge is a physical part with knuckles and a pin. A revolute joint only describes the turning movement in the model.
Align places a new shape at a point. A joint places a whole part against another part, and can do it again at any angle.

terms.name: Interference check
terms.keywords: overlap collide collision clash hit touch inside each other same space intersect fits check verify test
terms.summary: A test that no two parts of an assembly occupy the same space.
terms.definition: Two real parts cannot be in the same place, but two modelled parts can overlap with no warning at all. An interference check finds those overlaps. It intersects each pair of parts and measures the volume they share: zero means they are clear, and anything more is a clash that must be fixed. Run it every time parts are moved or changed.

say.text: Check every pair of parts in the assembly for overlap, and list each clash with its volume and where it is.
Does the {board} overlap the {base} anywhere? Show the overlapping volume in red.
The {board} clashes with the {right wall}. Fix it by {making the case 3 mm longer}, not by moving the board.
The screws overlap their threaded holes on purpose. Ignore those and report everything else.

terms.codeNote: (a & b).volume is the volume two parts share: 0 means no overlap. Parts that only touch share a face but no volume, so they pass.
terms.note: Passing the check does not mean the parts fit in real life. They also need clearance, because no printer is exact.

confusedWith.diff: An interference fit is an overlap you design on purpose, for a press fit. An interference check looks for overlaps you did not intend.
The check uses the intersect operation, but only to measure. It does not change the parts.

terms.name: Bought part
terms.keywords: buy purchased market shop standard component screw motor bearing sensor module battery connector datasheet dimensions real existing not printed hardware
terms.summary: A part you buy, modelled only so that your own parts can be designed to fit it.
terms.definition: A bought part is anything in the design that you do not make: screws, nuts, motors, bearings, batteries, circuit boards, aluminium profile. It goes into the model as reference geometry, so that the printed parts can be shaped around it and checked against it. Its size is fixed by its maker, so it is never changed and never printed. People who 3D print often call these parts vitamins.

say.text: This design uses a bought part: {an 18650 battery cell, 18.4 mm in diameter and 65.2 mm long}. Model it as a simple reference part. Never change its size and do not print it.
Build a stand-in for the {motor} from these datasheet numbers: {body 42.3 × 42.3 × 34 mm, shaft 5 mm, four M3 holes on a 31 mm square}. Only the outside shape and the mounting points matter.
I saved the maker's STEP file as {parts/motor.step}. Import it, tell me its overall size, and use it as the reference.
Design the {cradle} around the bought part with {0.4 mm} of clearance, and check that the two do not overlap.
Leave bought parts out of the files you export for printing, and list them separately as a shopping list.

terms.codeNote: Keep each bought part in its own function or file and give it a label. Use import_step() when the maker offers a STEP file. Otherwise a few Box and Cylinder shapes with the right outside sizes and hole positions are enough.
terms.note: Use the largest size the datasheet allows, not the typical one, and measure the part you actually have. Cheap parts often differ from their drawing.

confusedWith.diff: A bought part is a real object with a fixed shape. A keep-out zone is empty space you reserve, often around a bought part.
A STEP file is how the exact shape of a bought part usually reaches you. The bought part is the object itself.

terms.name: STEP, STL and 3MF
terms.keywords: file format save export import download share slicer triangles mesh exact stp step stl 3mf convert vendor model send
terms.summary: The file types for 3D models: STEP keeps the exact shape, STL and 3MF hold triangles for the slicer.
terms.definition: A STEP file (.step or .stp) stores the exact shape of a part: true flat faces, cylinders and curves. Any CAD program can open it and keep working on it, so it is the format for sharing designs, and for the models that makers publish of their motors, bearings and connectors. An STL file stores only a skin of small flat triangles, which is all a slicer needs for printing. 3MF is a newer format for the slicer that also stores the units, colours and several parts in one file.

say.text: Export each printed part as its own STL file into the {out} folder, in the orientation it will be printed.
Also export the whole assembly as one STEP file, so it can be opened in other CAD programs.
Import {parts/nema17.step}, tell me its overall size and where its origin is, and move it so that {the mounting face is at z = 0 with the shaft along +Z}.
Round surfaces look faceted in the print. Export the STL with a finer tolerance.

terms.codeNote: export_step(part, "name.step") and import_step("name.step") keep the exact shape. export_stl(part, "name.stl") makes triangles: a smaller tolerance= gives smoother curves and a larger file. For 3MF, use the Mesher class.
terms.printTip: The slicer needs STL or 3MF. Keep the Python script as the real source of the design, and use STEP for sharing. An STL cannot be turned back into a clean model that you can edit.

confusedWith.diff: A STEP file is a file. A bought part is the real object, whose shape often comes to you as a STEP file.

confusedWith.name: G-code
confusedWith.diff: STL and 3MF describe a shape. G-code is the list of movements that the slicer writes from that shape, for one particular printer.

terms.name: Aluminium extrusion
terms.keywords: frame rail beam bar profile 2020 2040 3030 4040 t-slot v-slot t-nut slot nut m5 bracket corner structure machine printer cnc 8020
terms.summary: Ready-made aluminium bars with slots along every side, used to build frames.
terms.definition: Aluminium extrusion is a bar with the same cross-section along its whole length, bought by the metre and cut to length. The common 2020 profile is 20 × 20 mm, with a T-shaped slot running down each of its four sides. A T-nut slides into a slot and turns it into a threaded hole anywhere along the bar, so printed parts can be bolted on and moved later. Bars are joined to each other with corner brackets.

say.text: The frame is made of 2020 aluminium extrusion. Model each bar as a bought part: {20 × 20 mm} with {6 mm} slots, cut to {300 mm}. Do not print it.
Design a printed {sensor mount} that bolts to one face of the bar with {two} M5 screws into T-nuts, {20 mm} apart along the slot.
Add a key {5.7 mm} wide and {1.2 mm} tall under the part, so it sits in the slot and the part cannot turn.
The part is {4 mm} thick where the screw passes through. Tell me which M5 screw length reaches the T-nut without touching the bottom of the slot.
Design a printed corner bracket that joins two bars at 90°, with {two} M5 screws into each bar.

terms.codeNote: The profile is one sketch extruded to the length of the bar. A simple stand-in with the 20 mm square, the four slots and the centre hole is enough to design against.
terms.printTip: Print a bracket so that the layers run along its arms, not across the bend. M5 screws pull hard: make the plastic under the head at least 4 mm thick, or add a washer.
terms.note: On a 2020 profile the slot opening is about 6 mm wide and about 6 mm deep, and the usual screw is M5. V-slot is the same idea with slanted slot edges for wheels to run on. Larger profiles such as 3030 and 4040 have wider slots and take larger screws: check the seller's drawing.

confusedWith.diff: Extrude is the CAD operation. An extrusion is a real metal bar, made in a factory by pushing aluminium through a shaped opening: the same idea in real life.
A nut trap is a pocket you print for an ordinary nut. A T-nut slides in the slot of the metal bar.

terms.name: Motor mount
terms.keywords: stepper motor nema 17 14 23 servo dc gear motor fix hold bracket plate face flange hole pattern pilot boss shaft 42 31 mounting actuator
terms.summary: The plate or bracket that holds a motor, with holes that match the face of the motor.
terms.definition: A motor mount is the part a motor is screwed to. Its holes must match the pattern on the face of the motor exactly, so the numbers come from the motor's drawing. A stepper motor is named by the size of its square face: a NEMA 17 has a 42.3 mm face, four M3 threaded holes on a 31 mm square, and a raised ring around the shaft called the boss or pilot. A hole for that ring in the mount centres the motor.

say.text: Make a mounting plate for a NEMA 17 stepper motor: a {22.5 mm} centre hole for the boss and four {3.4 mm} holes on a {31 mm} square, in a plate {4 mm} thick.
The holes in the motor are M3 threads, {4.5 mm} deep. For a {4 mm} plate use M3 × {8} screws, and counterbore the heads.
Turn the four screw holes into slots {6 mm} long, all in the same direction, so the motor can slide to tighten the belt.
Stand the plate upright on a base with two triangular ribs. The shaft points along {+Y}.
For the servo, cut a rectangular opening {23.2 × 13 mm} for its body and add two {1.6 mm} screw holes {27.8 mm} apart for its mounting ears. Check these numbers against my servo's drawing first.

table.caption: Stepper motor faces, in mm
table.note: Hole spacing is centre to centre, along the sides of a square. NEMA 14 and 17 have threaded holes in the motor. NEMA 23 has plain holes through its flange, so the screws need nuts or a thread in your part. Make the hole for the boss about 0.5 mm larger than the boss. The length of the body and of the shaft differ from model to model: take them from the datasheet.

terms.printTip: A working motor gets warm, often 50 to 70 °C, and PLA softens at about 60 °C. Print motor mounts in PETG, ABS or ASA.

confusedWith.diff: On a motor, the boss is the raised ring around the shaft that centres it. On a printed part, a boss is a raised post around a screw hole.
The mount holds the body of the motor still. The hub is the part that goes on the turning shaft.

terms.name: Shaft and hub
terms.keywords: axle rod spindle motor shaft flat d-cut d-shape wheel gear pulley knob fix slip spin set screw grub screw bore key coupler
terms.summary: The rod that turns, and the part with a hole that is fixed onto it.
terms.definition: A shaft is the rod that a motor turns. The hub is the centre of whatever goes on the shaft: a wheel, gear, pulley or knob. The hole through the hub is called the bore. A round shaft in a round bore just slips, so something must lock the two together. Many small shafts have one flat side, which makes a D shape, and a D-shaped bore cannot turn on it. A set screw through the side of the hub, pressing on the flat, stops the hub from sliding off.

say.text: Give the {knob} a D-shaped bore for a {5 mm} shaft that measures {4.5 mm} across the flat, with {0.1 mm} clearance, {10 mm} deep.
Add a {2.5 mm} hole through the side of the hub, aimed at the flat, for an {M3} set screw.
The motor shaft is {5 mm} in diameter and sticks out {22 mm}. The flat starts {5 mm} from the face of the motor.
Split the hub with a {1 mm} slot and put an {M3} screw across the slot, so that tightening the screw clamps the shaft.
Make the hub at least {3} times as wide as the shaft, so the plastic around the bore does not crack.

terms.codeNote: A D-shaped bore is a circle with a rectangle subtracted from it in the same sketch, then cut through the hub.
terms.printTip: Print the hub with the bore pointing up, so the bore is round and the layers are rings around the shaft. Start with 0.1 mm of clearance per side and test: a bore that is too tight splits the hub, and one that is too loose wobbles.

confusedWith.diff: A hub is fixed to the shaft and turns with it. A bearing lets the shaft turn inside a part that stays still.

terms.name: Bearing seat
terms.keywords: ball bearing 608 625 623 skate bearing spin turn smooth wheel shaft axle press fit pocket housing shoulder ring race
terms.summary: A round pocket that a ball bearing presses into, so a shaft can turn freely.
terms.definition: A ball bearing has an outer ring, an inner ring and balls between them, so the two rings turn against each other with almost no friction. A bearing seat is the round pocket in your part that holds the outer ring. It is as deep as the bearing is wide and very slightly tight, so the bearing presses in and stays. At the bottom is a ledge called a shoulder, which only the outer ring rests on. The inner ring and the shaft must touch nothing, so that they can turn.

say.text: Add a seat for a 608 bearing ({8 × 22 × 7 mm}) in the top face: {22.1 mm} wide and {7 mm} deep, with a {16 mm} through hole below it.
Make it a light press fit: the bearing should push in by hand and not fall out. Put the seat diameter in a parameter, so I can tune it.
Put one bearing seat at each end of the housing, on the same axis, {30 mm} apart.
Add a {0.5 mm} chamfer around the mouth of the seat.
Add a cover plate with {three M3} screws that holds the outer ring in its seat.

terms.codeNote: A bearing seat is a counterbore: CounterBoreHole with the seat as the wide part and the through hole as the narrow part.
terms.printTip: Print the seat with its opening facing up, so it comes out round. Printed holes come out small, so a seat modelled at exactly the size of the bearing is often a press fit already. Test with a thin ring before you print the whole part.

confusedWith.diff: The shape is the same. A counterbore hides a screw head. A bearing seat holds a bearing and must fit it closely.
A bearing lets a shaft turn freely. A hub is locked to the shaft and turns with it.
